title: Emperor Henry VI dies
text: Henry VI dies of fever at Messina; the empire falls into a contest between Philip of Swabia and Otto of Brunswick.

title: Innocent III elected pope
text: Lothar of Segni becomes Innocent III, the most powerful pope of the age, and soon calls a new crusade.

title: Two kings of the Romans
text: Rival princes elect Philip of Swabia and Otto IV; ten years of civil war follow across the German lands.

title: Ottokar I king of Bohemia
text: Premysl Ottokar I takes the title of king, which the Golden Bull of 1212 later confirms.

title: Richard the Lionheart dies
text: Richard I of England dies of a crossbow wound at the siege of Chalus; John takes the throne.

title: The Courts of Love take note
text: Philip II of France grows stronger against the English kings; the Toreador of the Grand Court watch the balance shift toward Paris.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The university of Paris chartered
text: Philip II grants the scholars of Paris rights against the city's officers, the start of the university's privileges.

title: Masters of the new university
text: Hermetic masters take rooms among the Paris scholars, and the craftsmen who will become the Order of Reason do the same.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Venice agrees to carry the crusade
text: The Treaty of Venice binds the Fourth Crusade to pay for a fleet it cannot afford.

title: Fibonacci's book of reckoning
text: Leonardo of Pisa publishes the Liber Abaci, bringing Hindu-Arabic numerals to European merchants.

title: The first crusader assault on Constantinople
text: Crusaders storm the city's sea walls and restore Isaac II and Alexios IV; the bargain cannot be paid.

title: The great fire of 1203
text: A fire set during fighting burns a broad swath of Constantinople; tens of thousands lose their homes.

title: Alexios V seizes the throne
text: Alexios Doukas Mourtzouphlos strangles Alexios IV and defies the crusaders.

title: Three days of sack
text: The crusaders break in and loot for three days; Cainites of every clan flee or burn with their havens, and the Dream ends.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Relics carried west
text: Relics, books and treasures from the sack flood into Venice, Paris and the Rhineland; mages hunt for the true ones among the fakes.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Empire of Nicaea
text: Theodore Laskaris gathers Byzantine refugees at Nicaea and founds a successor state.

title: The Empire of Trebizond
text: The Komnenos brothers found an empire on the Black Sea coast with Georgian help.

title: Normandy lost to France
text: Philip II takes Rouen and Normandy from King John.

title: Adrianople
text: The Bulgarian tsar Kaloyan destroys the Latin army and captures Emperor Baldwin I, who dies in prison.

title: The Delhi Sultanate
text: Qutb ud-Din Aibak, a slave general, founds the Mamluk dynasty of Delhi.

title: The khan's oath under the Eternal Blue Sky
text: Temujin is proclaimed Genghis Khan; the courts of the Middle Kingdom take the omens of the steppe seriously.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: England under interdict threat
text: Innocent III names Stephen Langton Archbishop of Canterbury against King John's wishes.

title: A legate murdered
text: The papal legate Peter of Castelnau is killed near Saint-Gilles; the pope calls a crusade against the Cathars.

title: England under interdict
text: The pope lays England under interdict: no masses, no church burials, for six years.

title: Francis of Assisi's first rule
text: Pope Innocent approves the brotherhood of Francis; the Franciscans begin.

title: Carcassonne falls
text: Simon de Montfort takes Carcassonne; inquirers ride with the army and learn which questions make people confess.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Aristotle banned
text: A council at Paris forbids lecturing on Aristotle's natural philosophy; the ban is widely ignored.

title: The Mongols attack the Jin
text: Genghis Khan invades the Jin empire and wins at Badger Mouth.

title: The Teutonic Knights in Transylvania
text: King Andrew II of Hungary settles the Teutonic Order in the Burzenland to guard the passes.

title: Las Navas de Tolosa
text: Christian kings of Spain crush the Almohads; the reconquest of al-Andalus speeds up.

title: The children's crusade passes
text: Bands of children and the poor march toward the sea; few come home, and some Kindred along the road grow fat.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Muret
text: Simon de Montfort kills Peter II of Aragon at Muret; the south loses its strongest protector.

title: Bouvines
text: Philip II beats Otto IV and his allies; John's hopes of retaking Normandy end, and Otto's empire collapses.

title: Zhongdu falls
text: The Mongols take the Jin capital (Beijing) and burn it for a month.

title: The Fourth Lateran Council
text: The council requires yearly confession, defines transubstantiation and orders Jews and Muslims to wear distinct dress.

title: King John dies
text: John dies during the barons' war; the boy Henry III is crowned and William Marshal rules for him.

title: The Dominicans approved
text: Pope Honorius III confirms the Order of Preachers founded by Dominic.

title: The Fair of Lincoln
text: William Marshal routs the French-backed rebels at Lincoln; Prince Louis gives up the English crown.

title: The Fifth Crusade sails
text: Crusaders gather at Acre, then turn on Egypt.

title: The Otrar killing
text: The governor of Otrar kills a Mongol trade caravan; Genghis Khan resolves on war with Khwarazm.

title: Damietta falls
text: The crusaders take Damietta after a long siege; disease has killed most of the city.

title: The riders cross the Jaxartes
text: The Mongol host enters Khwarazm; Garou of the Silk Road watch the land fill with ash and carrion spirits.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Samarkand falls
text: Samarkand surrenders and is plundered; its craftsmen are carried off to Mongolia.

title: The killing at Merv
text: Tolui's army takes Merv and kills nearly every inhabitant; chroniclers write of hundreds of thousands dead.

title: Nishapur destroyed
text: After a Mongol prince dies in its siege, Nishapur is razed and even its animals killed.

title: The Fifth Crusade ends
text: The crusaders, trapped by the Nile's flood, give up Damietta.

title: The Battle of the Indus
text: Jalal al-Din of Khwarazm escapes Genghis Khan by riding his horse into the river.

title: The Golden Bull of Hungary
text: Andrew II grants the Hungarian nobles their rights, including the right to resist an unjust king.

links.title: Hungary and the Slavic East in 1230

title: The university of Padua
text: Scholars leaving Bologna found a new school at Padua.

title: The Kalka
text: Mongol scouts under Subutai destroy the Rus princes on the Kalka; the Rus forget the warning, and the Shadow Lords do not.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Philip Augustus dies
text: Philip II of France dies after 43 years; Louis VIII takes the throne.

title: Frederick II founds Naples university
text: The emperor founds a school at Naples to train lawyers and officials for his kingdom.

title: The stigmata of Francis
text: Francis of Assisi is said to receive the wounds of Christ; the Messianic Voices count it a sign.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Magna Carta reissued
text: Henry III reissues Magna Carta in its lasting form in return for a tax.

title: Francis of Assisi dies
text: Francis dies at the Portiuncula; canonised two years later.

title: Louis VIII dies
text: The king dies on his way back from the Albigensian campaign; Blanche of Castile rules for the boy Louis IX.

title: Genghis Khan dies
text: Genghis Khan dies during the war on the Xi Xia, who are destroyed; the courts of the East mark the death of the scourge.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Bornhoved
text: North German princes break Danish power in the Baltic.

title: The Sixth Crusade
text: Excommunicated, Frederick II sails for the Holy Land anyway.

title: Jerusalem returned by treaty
text: Sultan al-Kamil hands Jerusalem to Frederick II by treaty, without a battle.

title: The Treaty of Paris
text: The Albigensian war ends; Toulouse submits and the Inquisition arrives in the south.

title: The council of Toulouse
text: A church council at Toulouse sets out how to search out heretics and bans the Bible in the common tongue.

title: Castile and Leon united
text: Ferdinand III unites the crowns of Castile and Leon for good.

title: The Teutonic crusade in Prussia
text: The Teutonic Knights begin their war against the pagan Prussians from Kulm.

title: Papal inquisitors
text: Gregory IX sends inquisitors answerable to the pope, most of them Dominicans.

title: The Constitutions of Melfi
text: Frederick II issues a law code for the Kingdom of Sicily.

title: Conrad of Marburg's hunt
text: Conrad of Marburg burns suspects across Germany; the shadow Inquisition in the Empire takes note of his methods.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Conrad of Marburg murdered
text: Knights kill the inquisitor on the road; his terror ends.

title: The end of the Jin
text: The Mongols and the Song take the last Jin city; the last Jin emperor dies.

title: Karakorum walled
text: Ogedei Khan builds walls and a palace at Karakorum, the Mongol capital.

title: Cordoba taken
text: Ferdinand III takes Cordoba; the great mosque becomes a cathedral.

title: The Mongols turn west
text: Batu and Subutai destroy Volga Bulgaria.

title: Ryazan burned
text: The first Rus city falls to Batu's host.

title: Vladimir falls
text: The Mongols take Vladimir and burn the grand prince's family in the cathedral.

title: The Sit River
text: Grand Prince Yuri II is killed and his army destroyed.

title: Valencia taken
text: James I of Aragon takes Valencia.

title: Frederick II excommunicated again
text: Pope and emperor go to open war in Italy.

title: The Neva
text: Prince Alexander of Novgorod beats a Swedish force and is called Nevsky.

title: Kiev falls
text: Batu's army storms Kiev; the mother of Rus cities is ruined, and Cainites who held it scatter.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Krakow burned
text: A Mongol column burns Krakow; legend says a trumpeter was shot mid-call from the church tower.

title: Legnica
text: The Mongols destroy Duke Henry II of Silesia's army, Teutonic and Templar knights among it.

title: Mohi
text: Batu and Subutai destroy the Hungarian army; King Bela IV flees to the Adriatic.

title: Ogedei dies and the horde turns back
text: Word of the great khan's death reaches the army in Hungary; the Mongols withdraw, and the Tzimisce and the Garou of the plains count their dead.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

links.title: Hungary and the Slavic East in 1230

title: Lubeck and Hamburg ally
text: The two cities agree to guard the road between them, the seed of the Hanseatic League.

title: The battle on the ice
text: Alexander Nevsky beats the Livonian Knights on frozen Lake Peipus.

title: The Golden Horde
text: Batu sets his capital at Sarai on the Volga; the Rus princes must travel there for leave to rule.

title: Kose Dag
text: The Mongols break the Seljuk sultanate of Rum.

title: The fall of Montsegur
text: More than two hundred Cathars are burned below the mountain fortress; the Inquisition calls it victory, and the Inquisition is wrong to call it the end.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Jerusalem sacked
text: Khwarazmian horsemen take and wreck Jerusalem.

links.title: Cainites under the Kingdom of Jerusalem
Gabriel Chavez, the Eyes of Alamut

title: La Forbie
text: An Egyptian and Khwarazmian army destroys the crusader host near Gaza.

title: Frederick II deposed
text: The Council of Lyon declares the emperor deposed.

title: A friar to the khan
text: John of Plano Carpini sets out for the Mongol court as the pope's envoy.

title: Guyuk enthroned
text: Guyuk becomes great khan with Carpini watching.

title: Seville taken
text: Ferdinand III takes Seville after a long siege.

title: Cologne cathedral begun
text: The foundation stone of the new cathedral is laid; it will not be finished for six hundred years.

title: The Sainte-Chapelle
text: Louis IX consecrates his glass chapel for the Crown of Thorns; the Celestial Chorus calls it a true house of the One.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Seventh Crusade lands
text: Louis IX takes Damietta again.

title: Mansourah
text: The crusaders break into Mansourah and are cut down in its streets by the Mamluks under Baibars.

title: Louis IX captured
text: The French king is taken prisoner and ransomed.

title: The Mamluks take Egypt
text: Mamluk officers kill the last Ayyubid sultan of Egypt.

title: Frederick II dies
text: The stupor mundi dies in Apulia; Hohenstaufen power soon collapses.

title: Mongke becomes great khan
text: After a bitter assembly Mongke is raised as great khan and purges Ogedei's line.

title: The gold florin
text: Florence strikes the gold florin, soon the standard coin of European trade.

title: William of Rubruck at Karakorum
text: The Flemish friar reaches the great khan's court and debates Buddhists, Muslims and Nestorians there.

title: The kingdom of Dali falls
text: Kublai conquers the kingdom of Dali in Yunnan.

title: The Great Interregnum
text: With Conrad IV dead, the empire has no accepted ruler for almost twenty years.

title: The Rhenish League
text: Rhineland towns band together to keep the peace on the river roads.

title: The Nizari castles surrender
text: Hulegu takes Alamut and the Nizari strongholds; Kindred in the east say the Assamites did not stir, because their Alamut is not this one.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

links.title: Gabriel Chavez, the Eyes of Alamut

title: The Sorbonne
text: Robert de Sorbon founds a college for poor theology students in Paris.

title: Baghdad sacked
text: The Mongols take Baghdad, kill the caliph and throw the libraries into the Tigris; Batini carry out what they can.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Provisions of Oxford
text: English barons force Henry III to share power with a council.

title: Rumi's poems
text: Jalal ad-Din Rumi begins the Masnavi at Konya.

title: The Treaty of Paris
text: Henry III gives up his claims to Normandy and Anjou and keeps Gascony as Louis IX's vassal.

title: Aleppo and Damascus fall
text: Hulegu takes Aleppo and Damascus; the Mamluks are next.

title: Ain Jalut
text: The Mamluks under Qutuz and Baibars beat the Mongols in Galilee; the mummies of Egypt call it a reprieve for the river.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Baibars becomes sultan
text: Baibars murders Qutuz on the road home and takes the throne.

title: Kressenbrunn
text: Ottokar II of Bohemia beats the Hungarians and takes Styria.

title: The flagellants
text: Bands of penitents whip themselves through the towns of Italy; the Church is unsure whether to bless them or hunt them.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Kublai and Ariq Boke
text: Kublai and his brother Ariq Boke are both proclaimed great khan; civil war splits the empire.

title: The Byzantines take back the city
text: Michael VIII Palaiologos's general walks into Constantinople almost without a fight; Latin rule ends, but the Dream does not return.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Iceland under Norway
text: The Icelandic chieftains accept the Norwegian king.

title: Largs
text: Scots and storms drive off a Norwegian fleet; the Hebrides pass to Scotland three years later.

title: Lewes
text: Simon de Montfort captures Henry III and his son Edward.

title: Corpus Christi
text: Urban IV makes the feast of Corpus Christi a feast of the whole Church.

title: Montfort's parliament
text: Simon de Montfort calls knights and burgesses from towns to parliament.

title: Evesham
text: Prince Edward kills Simon de Montfort and cuts the body to pieces.

title: Benevento
text: Charles of Anjou kills King Manfred and takes Sicily and Naples.

title: Roger Bacon writes for the pope
text: Roger Bacon sends Clement IV his great work on experiment and optics; the craftsmen of the future Order of Reason study it.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Giotto born
text: The painter Giotto di Bondone is born near Florence.

title: The last Hohenstaufen
text: Charles of Anjou defeats Conradin, then beheads the sixteen-year-old in Naples.

title: Antioch destroyed
text: Baibars takes Antioch and kills or enslaves its people; the crusader principality ends.

title: Louis IX dies at Tunis
text: The Eighth Crusade ends when the French king dies of dysentery outside Tunis.

title: The Yuan dynasty
text: Kublai Khan proclaims the Great Yuan and builds a new capital at Khanbaliq (Beijing).

title: The Polos set out
text: Marco Polo leaves Venice with his father and uncle for the court of Kublai.

title: Krak des Chevaliers falls
text: The Hospitallers give up their great castle to Baibars.

title: Henry III dies
text: Edward I becomes king of England while still on crusade.

title: Rudolf of Habsburg elected
text: The German princes choose Rudolf of Habsburg as king, ending the interregnum.

title: Rumi dies
text: The poet dies at Konya; the whirling dervishes of the Mevlevi order grow from his followers.

title: Thomas Aquinas dies
text: Aquinas dies on the way to the Council of Lyon, his Summa unfinished.

title: The first Mongol fleet against Japan
text: A Mongol and Korean fleet lands at Hakata and then sails off in a storm; the kami are said to have answered.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Second Council of Lyon
text: The Greek envoys accept union with Rome; their church at home does not.

title: Hangzhou surrenders
text: The Song capital surrenders to the Mongol general Bayan.

title: The Paris condemnations
text: Bishop Tempier condemns 219 philosophical propositions, many drawn from Aristotle and Averroes.

title: Edward I invades Wales
text: Llywelyn ap Gruffudd is forced to terms.

title: The Marchfeld
text: Rudolf of Habsburg kills Ottokar II of Bohemia; Austria passes to the Habsburgs.

title: The fall of the Song
text: The last Song fleet is destroyed at Yamen and the boy emperor drowns; Kuei-jin speak of a turning of the age.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Albertus Magnus dies
text: The Dominican master of natural philosophy dies at Cologne.

title: The divine wind
text: A typhoon wrecks the second, far larger Mongol invasion of Japan; priests and spirits both claim the storm.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Sicilian Vespers
text: Palermo rises against the French at vespers on Easter Monday; Sicily passes to Aragon.

title: Llywelyn killed
text: The last native Prince of Wales dies in a skirmish; Wales is conquered.

title: Edward's castles
text: Edward I begins Caernarfon, Conwy and Harlech to hold Wales.

title: Prussia conquered
text: The Teutonic Knights finish the conquest of the Prussians.

title: Meloria
text: Genoa destroys the Pisan fleet; Pisa never recovers.

title: The children of Hamelin
text: One hundred and thirty children vanish from Hamelin; the town's records blame a piper, and the fae say nothing.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Philip the Fair
text: Philip IV becomes King of France.

title: St. Lucia's flood
text: A storm surge drowns tens of thousands along the Dutch and German coast.

title: Worringen
text: The burghers of Cologne and their allies break the archbishop's power.

title: Tripoli falls
text: The Mamluks take Tripoli in Lebanon.

title: The Jews expelled from England
text: Edward I orders all Jews out of England; they will not be readmitted for over three centuries.

title: Acre falls
text: The Mamluks storm Acre and the crusader kingdom ends; Kindred of the Military Orders sail for Cyprus with the survivors.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Swiss oath
text: Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden swear to defend each other, the start of the Swiss Confederation.

title: The Mongols in Java
text: A Mongol fleet lands in Java; the Majapahit state rises from the fighting.

title: Celestine V resigns
text: The hermit pope resigns after five months; Boniface VIII follows him.

title: Kublai Khan dies
text: The great khan dies; his empire no longer obeys one ruler.

title: Ghazan turns to Islam
text: The Ilkhan Ghazan becomes Muslim, and the Mongols of Persia follow.

title: Marco Polo returns
text: The Polos come home to Venice after twenty-four years.

title: Berwick sacked
text: Edward I takes Berwick and kills many of its people; Scotland is conquered.

title: Stirling Bridge
text: William Wallace and Andrew Moray destroy an English army.

title: Falkirk
text: Edward I breaks Wallace's army.

title: Marco Polo's book
text: A prisoner of Genoa, Marco Polo tells his travels to the writer Rustichello.

title: Osman's beylik
text: Osman's frontier state in Bithynia grows; the Ottomans take their name from him.

title: Wadi al-Khazandar
text: Ghazan's Mongols beat the Mamluks near Homs and briefly take Damascus.

title: The first Jubilee
text: Boniface VIII proclaims a holy year; pilgrims crowd Rome for full pardon of sins.

title: The Prague groschen
text: Wenceslas II reforms the Bohemian coinage on Kutna Hora silver.

title: Dante exiled
text: Dante Alighieri is banished from Florence and begins the Divine Comedy in exile.

title: The Bruges Matins
text: Flemish townsmen kill the French garrison of Bruges at dawn.

title: The Golden Spurs
text: Flemish militia destroy the French knights at Courtrai.

title: Unam Sanctam
text: Boniface VIII declares that every creature must be subject to the pope.

title: Bapheus
text: Osman beats a Byzantine army, his first great victory.

title: The outrage at Anagni
text: Philip the Fair's men seize Boniface VIII; the pope dies weeks later.

title: Marj al-Saffar
text: The Mamluks beat Ghazan's last invasion of Syria.

title: The courts make peace
text: In the year the Quincunx is signed, mortal China lies quiet under the Yuan; the courts take it as proof the treaty works.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Wallace executed
text: William Wallace is hanged, drawn and quartered at Smithfield.

title: Robert the Bruce crowned
text: Robert Bruce kills a rival and is crowned King of Scots.

title: The Jews expelled from France
text: Philip IV expels the Jews from France and takes their goods.

title: The last Premyslid
text: Wenceslas III is murdered at Olomouc; the Bohemian royal line ends.

title: The Templars arrested
text: On Friday 13 October Philip IV has every Templar in France seized; some say Cainite counsellors or Batini with grudges guided the king.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Edward I dies
text: Edward I dies on his way north to fight Bruce; Edward II takes the throne.

title: Danzig taken
text: The Teutonic Knights seize Danzig and kill many of its people.

title: The popes at Avignon
text: Clement V settles in Avignon; the popes will stay for nearly seventy years, and the Kindred of Rome lose their nearest grip on the Church.

title: Marienburg
text: The Teutonic grand master moves to Marienburg, the largest brick castle in Europe.

title: The Hospitallers take Rhodes
text: The Knights of St John make Rhodes their island base.

title: The Council of Vienne
text: The council meets to decide the fate of the Templars.

title: The Templars suppressed
text: Clement V dissolves the Order of the Temple and gives its lands to the Hospitallers.

title: Henry VII dies in Italy
text: The emperor dies of fever, ending hopes of restoring imperial rule in Italy.

title: Jacques de Molay burns
text: The last Grand Master is burned on an island in the Seine; the tale of a curse on king and pope spreads when both die that year.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Bannockburn
text: Robert Bruce routs Edward II's army.

title: The Great Famine
text: Years of rain ruin the harvests of northern Europe; as many as one in ten die by 1317.

title: Morgarten
text: Swiss peasants ambush and destroy a Habsburg army.

title: Solificati
text: De Varre founds the Solificati, the alchemists who will break away from the Order of Reason.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: John XXII elected
text: The Avignon pope who will condemn magic and the Spiritual Franciscans takes office.

title: The Kindred hunger too
text: With the herds starving, Kindred across the north feed on the dying and the Masquerade frays in the poorhouses.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Four Franciscans burned
text: Four Spiritual Franciscans who would not give up their poverty are burned at Marseille.

title: The Declaration of Arbroath
text: Scottish nobles ask the pope to recognise their independence.

title: The Shepherds' Crusade
text: Bands of young shepherds march south and massacre Jews; the authorities crush them.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The lepers' plot
text: Rumour claims lepers poisoned the wells for the Jews and the king of Granada; lepers are burned across France.

title: Dante dies
text: Dante dies in exile at Ravenna, the Comedy complete.

title: Muhldorf
text: Louis of Bavaria captures his rival Frederick of Austria.

title: The Flemish peasants rise
text: Coastal Flanders rises against taxes and lords for five years.

title: Mansa Musa in Cairo
text: Mansa Musa passes through Cairo with so much gold that its price falls for years.

title: Alice Kyteler tried
text: The first witch trial in Ireland; Alice Kyteler escapes to England and a servant is burned in her place. Verbena in Ireland grow careful.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Ibn Battuta sets out
text: Ibn Battuta leaves Tangier on pilgrimage and travels for nearly thirty years.

title: The Order of Reason founded
text: In the year the Convention of the White Tower meets, the Order of Reason takes its name.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Bursa taken
text: Orhan takes Bursa and makes it the Ottoman capital.

title: Edward II murdered
text: The deposed king dies in prison; Edward III, fourteen, takes the throne.

title: The Valois
text: Charles IV dies without a son; Philip VI of Valois takes the crown, and Edward III's claim waits.

title: Cassel
text: Philip VI crushes the Flemish rising.

title: Louis of Bavaria crowned in Rome
text: Louis IV is crowned emperor by the Roman people and sets up an antipope.

title: Pelekanos
text: Orhan beats the Byzantine emperor in Bithynia.

title: The Paris University Purge
text: Mages die and the Hermetic covenant of Le Ictus is destroyed in the purge of 1330; the scholars of the city never learn why their colleagues vanished.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Nicaea falls
text: The Ottomans take Nicaea.

title: Plague in China
text: An epidemic kills many in Hebei; some historians see the first sign of the Black Death.

title: The Genko War
text: Emperor Go-Daigo rises against the Kamakura shogunate.

title: Kamakura falls
text: Nitta Yoshisada takes Kamakura; the Hojo regents kill themselves and the shogunate ends.

title: Halidon Hill
text: Edward III's archers destroy a Scottish army.

title: The Arno flood
text: The Arno sweeps away Florence's bridges.

title: Giotto's bell tower
text: Giotto begins the campanile of Florence cathedral.

title: The Ilkhanate breaks up
text: Abu Said dies without an heir; Mongol Persia falls apart.

title: Two courts in Japan
text: Ashikaga Takauji takes Kyoto; Go-Daigo flees to Yoshino, and the Northern and Southern courts begin.

title: Vijayanagara founded
text: Harihara and Bukka found the empire of Vijayanagara in southern India.

title: The Hundred Years War begins
text: Philip VI confiscates Gascony; Edward III claims the French crown.

title: Giotto dies
text: The painter who changed Italian art dies in Florence.

title: The Ashikaga shogunate
text: Ashikaga Takauji becomes shogun.

title: The Declaration of Rhens
text: The electors declare that the man they choose is king without the pope's leave.

title: Venice and Florence fight Verona
text: Venice expands on the mainland at Verona's cost.

title: Sluys
text: The English destroy the French fleet off Flanders.

title: Rio Salado
text: Castile and Portugal beat the last great Marinid invasion of Spain.

title: Byzantine civil war

title: Victoria dies
text: The queen dies at Osborne after sixty-three years, and Edward VII takes the throne.

title: The wireless crosses
text: Marconi receives a radio signal sent from Cornwall across the Atlantic.

title: The D'Arcy oil concession
text: Persia grants a British prospector the right to drill for oil across most of the country.

title: The Brno technical college
text: The Czech technical university opens in Brno.

title: The Anglo-Japanese Alliance
text: Britain ends its splendid isolation in an alliance with Japan.

title: The campanile falls
text: The bell tower of St Mark's in Venice collapses into a heap of rubble.

title: Siam modernises
text: King Chulalongkorn's reforms keep Siam independent between British and French empires.

title: The suffragettes
text: Emmeline Pankhurst founds the Women's Social and Political Union: deeds, not words.

title: The May coup
text: Officers murder King Alexander and Queen Draga of Serbia and throw their bodies from a window.

title: The Kishinev pogrom
text: A mob kills forty-nine Jews over two days in Bessarabia while police watch.

title: The Ilinden rising
text: Macedonian revolutionaries rise against the Ottomans and are crushed with village burnings.

title: Bolsheviks and Mensheviks
text: Russian socialists split at their London congress, and Lenin's faction calls itself the majority.

title: The Russo-Japanese War
text: Japan attacks the Russian fleet at Port Arthur without warning and lays siege to the port.

title: The Entente Cordiale
text: Britain and France settle their colonial quarrels and draw together against Germany.

title: The Hejaz Railway
text: Work presses on the railway from Damascus to Medina, built for the hajj.

title: Bloody Sunday
text: Troops fire on workers marching to petition the tsar, and revolution spreads across Russia.

title: Tsushima
text: Japan destroys the Russian Baltic fleet after its voyage around the world.

title: Mukden
text: Over half a million men fight for three weeks outside Mukden, the largest battle the world has yet seen.

title: The Potemkin mutiny
text: Sailors on the battleship Potemkin mutiny over rotten meat and sail to Odessa.

title: The October Manifesto
text: The tsar promises a parliament and civil rights to end the general strike.

title: The miracle year
text: A patent clerk named Einstein publishes on light, atoms and special relativity in one year.

title: The Brno university riots
text: Germans and Czechs clash over a Czech university in Brno; a joiner, Frantisek Pavlik, is killed by troops on the steps of the House of Artists.

title: The Persian constitutional revolution
text: Merchants and clerics take sanctuary and force the shah to grant a parliament.

title: The Kangra earthquake
text: An earthquake in the Himalayan foothills kills twenty thousand.

title: Dreadnought
text: Britain launches an all big-gun battleship that makes every other warship obsolete.

title: The Courrieres mine disaster
text: A coal dust explosion in northern France kills over a thousand miners.

title: Vesuvius erupts
text: Vesuvius erupts, kills over a hundred, and sends Rome's Olympics to London.

title: The Persian parliament
text: The first Majlis meets in Tehran.

title: Bengal partitioned
text: Lord Curzon divides Bengal, and the boycott of British goods begins.

title: Universal male suffrage
text: Austria gives every man the vote for the Reichsrat, and Czech and socialist members flood in.

title: The Anglo-Russian Convention
text: Britain and Russia divide Persia into spheres and settle Afghanistan and Tibet.

title: Les Demoiselles d'Avignon
text: Picasso paints the canvas that opens the way to cubism.

title: The Tiflis bank robbery
text: Bolsheviks led by Kamo and organised by a young Stalin rob a bank convoy with bombs.

title: Bosnia annexed
text: Austria-Hungary annexes Bosnia and Herzegovina outright, and Serbia and Russia are humiliated.

title: The Young Turks
text: Ottoman officers in Macedonia force the sultan to bring back the constitution.

title: Tunguska
text: Something explodes over the Siberian forest and flattens eighty million trees.

title: The Messina earthquake
text: An earthquake and tsunami destroy Messina and Reggio and kill some eighty thousand.

title: Martial law in Prague

title: Oil struck in Persia
text: D'Arcy's drillers strike oil at Masjed Soleyman, and the Anglo-Persian Oil Company follows.

title: Bleriot crosses
text: Louis Bleriot flies across the English Channel.

title: Abdulhamid deposed

title: Edward VII dies

title: Korea annexed
text: Japan annexes Korea.

title: The Portuguese Republic
text: A revolution ends the monarchy in Portugal.

title: The Manchurian plague
text: Pneumonic plague kills sixty thousand in Manchuria until a Malayan doctor's masks and quarantines stop it.

title: Halley's comet
text: The earth passes through the comet's tail, and people buy comet pills against poison gas.

title: The Xinhai Revolution

title: The Delhi durbar
text: George V and Queen Mary are crowned emperor and empress of India in Delhi, and the capital moves from Calcutta.

title: Italy invades Libya
text: Italy attacks the Ottoman provinces of Libya; aircraft drop bombs in war for the first time.

title: The Mona Lisa stolen
text: The Mona Lisa vanishes from the Louvre; it turns up two years later in Florence.

title: The Agadir crisis
text: A German gunboat at Agadir nearly brings war with France over Morocco.

title: The fires of Istanbul
text: Great fires burn thousands of wooden houses in Istanbul.

title: The Titanic sinks
text: The liner strikes an iceberg on its first voyage; over fifteen hundred die.

title: The First Balkan War
text: Serbia, Bulgaria, Greece and Montenegro drive the Ottomans almost out of Europe.

title: The Meiji emperor dies
text: The Meiji emperor dies and General Nogi and his wife follow in ritual suicide.

title: The last emperor abdicates
text: The six-year-old Puyi gives up the throne, and China becomes a republic.

title: The Stockholm Olympics
text: The Stockholm Games bring electric timing and a photo finish.

title: Expressionism in Brno
text: Brno's Czech and German artists hold rival shows, and the town's cafes argue about modern art.

title: Albania declares independence
text: Ismail Qemali proclaims an independent Albania at Vlore.

title: The Second Balkan War
text: Bulgaria attacks its allies over Macedonia and loses.

title: The Redl affair
text: Colonel Redl, chief of Austrian counter-intelligence, is found to be a Russian spy and shoots himself.

title: The Rite of Spring
text: Stravinsky's ballet starts a riot in the theatre.

title: Emily Davison at the Derby

text: Austrian monitors on the Danube shell Belgrade the night after war is declared.

text: Belgium's forts at Liege hold the German advance for days until giant siege howitzers crush them.

title: Tannenberg
text: Hindenburg and Ludendorff encircle a Russian army in East Prussia; its general shoots himself.

title: The Battle of the Frontiers
text: French infantry in red trousers attack into Lorraine and the Ardennes and lose over a quarter of a million men in weeks.

title: Mons

text: Russia routs the Austro-Hungarian armies in Galicia and takes Lemberg; Austria loses four hundred thousand men in a month.

title: Heligoland Bight
text: British battlecruisers sink three German cruisers in the first sea fight of the war, near Heligoland.

title: The Marne
text: The French and British stop the Germans on the Marne, some reserves rushed out from Paris in taxis.

title: The first trenches

title: The siege of Przemysl
text: The Russians besiege the great Austrian fortress of Przemysl in Galicia.

title: The Masurian Lakes
text: Germany drives a second Russian army out of East Prussia.

title: Three cruisers sunk
text: One German submarine sinks three British cruisers in an hour.

title: Antwerp falls
text: The Belgian army slips out of Antwerp, and the city surrenders.

title: First Ypres
text: German volunteer regiments of students attack at Ypres and are shot down in thousands.

title: The Emden at Penang
text: The German raider Emden slips into Penang harbour and sinks a Russian cruiser before being hunted down.

title: Tsingtao falls
text: Japanese and British troops take Germany's Chinese port after a siege.

title: Belgrade taken
text: Austria takes Belgrade.

title: The landing at Fao

title: Kolubara
text: Serbia counterattacks at the Kolubara and drives the Austrians out of the country.

title: Sarikamish

title: Limanowa

title: Masaryk goes abroad

title: The sultan of Egypt

title: Czech papers silenced
text: Censorship closes Czech papers, and suspected Russophiles are arrested.

title: The manifesto of the ninety-three
text: German professors sign a manifesto defending the army in Belgium.

text: Britain gives its government wide powers over press, pubs and land.

title: Egypt a protectorate
text: Britain declares a protectorate over Egypt and deposes the khedive.

title: The hajj cut off
text: War closes the pilgrim roads, and few pilgrims reach Mecca.

title: Galicia's Jews flee
text: Russian troops in Galicia attack Jewish towns; hundreds of thousands flee to Vienna and Budapest.

title: The Thalerhof camp
text: Austria interns thousands of suspect Ruthenians in a camp near Graz, where many die.

title: Afghanistan neutral
text: The Afghan emir keeps out of the war despite Ottoman and German pleading.

title: The Carpathian winter
text: Austria attacks through the Carpathian passes in winter to relieve Przemysl and loses six hundred thousand men to battle and frost.

title: The attack on Suez
text: An Ottoman force crosses Sinai and tries to cross the canal; it is beaten off.

title: Dogger Bank
text: British and German battlecruisers fight off the Dogger Bank; the Blucher sinks.

title: Gas at Bolimow
text: Germany fires gas shells at the Russians at Bolimow; the cold stops the gas from working.

title: Tabriz changes hands
text: Ottoman and Russian forces fight over Tabriz in neutral Persia.

title: Unrestricted submarine war
text: Germany declares the waters round Britain a war zone where any ship may be sunk.

title: The Dardanelles shelled
text: British and French battleships begin shelling the forts at the mouth of the Dardanelles.

title: The naval attack fails
text: Mines sink three Allied battleships in the narrows in an afternoon, and the fleet withdraws.

title: Przemysl surrenders
text: The starving garrison of Przemysl blows up its forts and surrenders: over a hundred thousand prisoners.

title: Neuve Chapelle
text: The British break into the German line at Neuve Chapelle and cannot go further.

title: The Czech Mafia
text: Czech politicians at home form a secret network, called the Maffie, to send news to Masaryk abroad.

title: Chlorine at Ypres
text: Germany releases chlorine gas from cylinders at Ypres; French colonial troops break and the Canadians hold.

title: The Gallipoli landings
text: British, Australian, New Zealand and French troops land on Gallipoli; Mustafa Kemal holds the heights.

title: The Armenian deportations
text: Armenian leaders in Istanbul are arrested and killed, and the deportations of the Armenian people begin; about a million die.

title: The marches of the dead

title: The defence of Van
text: The Armenians of Van hold their quarter against Ottoman troops for a month until the Russians come.

title: The 28th regiment
text: The Prague 28th infantry regiment goes over to the Russians nearly whole in the Carpathians, and the army disbands it in disgrace.

title: Gorlice-Tarnow
text: German and Austrian armies break the Russian front at Gorlice, and the great retreat begins.

title: The Lusitania sunk
text: A German submarine sinks the liner Lusitania off Ireland; nearly twelve hundred die.

title: Italy declares war
text: Italy joins the Allies on promises of Austrian land.

title: Second Ypres ends
text: Second Ypres ends with the salient smaller and poisoned.

title: The first Isonzo
text: Italy attacks across the Isonzo river, the first of twelve battles there.

title: Lemberg retaken
text: Austria takes back Lemberg.

title: Kramar arrested
text: The Czech politician Karel Kramar is arrested for treason and later sentenced to death; the sentence is commuted.

title: Hus remembered
text: Masaryk in Geneva declares war on Austria on the five hundredth anniversary of Jan Hus's burning.

title: The second Isonzo
text: Italy attacks again on the Carso and loses forty thousand men.

title: Warsaw falls
text: The Germans take Warsaw as the Russians retreat, burning crops and driving civilians east.

title: Suvla Bay
text: A new British landing at Suvla Bay stalls on the beach.

title: The great retreat
text: Millions of refugees flee eastward ahead of the Russian armies through the summer.

title: Loos
text: Britain uses gas for the first time at Loos; the wind blows some of it back.

title: The Champagne offensive
text: France attacks in Champagne with huge losses for a few miles.

title: The Rovno offensive
text: Austria's autumn attack in Volhynia fails and costs it a quarter of a million men.

title: Serbia overrun
text: Germany, Austria and Bulgaria invade Serbia from three sides.

title: Edith Cavell shot
text: The Germans shoot the British nurse Edith Cavell for helping Allied soldiers escape.

title: The landing at Salonika
text: British and French troops land at Salonika in neutral Greece too late to save Serbia.

title: Ctesiphon
text: The British march on Baghdad is stopped at Ctesiphon, and the army falls back on Kut.

title: The retreat through Kosovo
text: Serbian civilians and soldiers stream across the Kosovo plain toward the mountains.

title: The Serbian retreat
text: The Serbian army and King Peter retreat through the Albanian mountains in winter; tens of thousands die.

title: The siege of Kut
text: The Ottomans surround the British at Kut.

title: Gallipoli evacuated
text: The Allies slip away from Gallipoli at night without losing a man, after eight months and half a million casualties.

title: The Arcanum's war
text: The house reading has the Arcanum in London lend scholars to naval intelligence and lose track of half its own members.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Twenty-One Demands
text: Japan demands control over much of China, and Chinese students boycott Japanese goods.

title: The Singapore mutiny
text: Indian troops in Singapore mutiny and kill Europeans before they are put down.

title: Letters from Mecca
text: Sharif Hussein of Mecca and the British high commissioner in Cairo begin letters on an Arab rising.

title: The Lebanon famine
text: An Allied blockade, locusts and Ottoman requisitions starve Mount Lebanon; perhaps half the people die.

title: The Carpathian Garou
text: The house reading has the Shadow Lords of the Carpathians wage their own war, using the armies to drive rival septs from caerns.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Bread cards in Vienna
text: Bread is rationed in Vienna, and queues begin outside every bakery.

title: Arab nationalists hanged
text: Jamal Pasha hangs Arab nationalists in Beirut and Damascus.

title: Zeppelin raids
text: German airships bomb London and English towns by night.

title: Lights out in London
text: The house reading has London's Kindred find the blackout a gift for hunting, and the prince orders discretion.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Good Soldier Svejk is born
text: In Prague cells and barracks Jaroslav Hasek gathers the material for the soldier who survives by seeming a fool.

title: The Niedermayer mission
text: A German and Ottoman mission reaches Kabul to raise Afghanistan against India and fails.

title: Wassmuss in Persia
text: A German agent called Wassmuss raises the southern Persian tribes against Britain.

title: Bulgaria joins
text: Bulgaria joins the Central Powers.

title: The great storm at Gallipoli
text: A blizzard and floods kill soldiers in the trenches at Suvla.

title: Montenegro falls
text: Austria takes Mount Lovcen and Montenegro surrenders.

title: Erzurum
text: Yudenich's Russians storm the fortress of Erzurum in the winter snows.

title: The Serbs on Corfu
text: The survivors of the Serbian army are shipped to Corfu, where thousands die of disease on Vido island.

title: Verdun
text: Germany attacks Verdun to bleed France white; the battle lasts ten months and costs some seven hundred thousand casualties.

title: The Verdun Shadowlands
text: The house reading has the Shadowlands of Verdun turn to a sea of mud and ghosts where Spectres hunt the newly dead.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Feeding at the front
text: The house reading has Kindred haunt the dressing stations behind Verdun, and the Camarilla struggles to stop Masquerade breaches among the dying.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The fifth Isonzo
text: Italy attacks again on the Isonzo with little gain.

title: Le Mort Homme
text: French and German troops fight for months over a hill called Dead Man.

title: The Easter Rising
text: Irish republicans seize the Dublin General Post Office and proclaim a republic; the leaders are shot after the surrender.

title: The Rising and the Dreaming
text: The house reading has the Irish Kithain see the Rising as a poem made real, and the Unseelie mourn its poets.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Kut surrenders
text: The starving British at Kut surrender; many of the prisoners die on the march into Anatolia.

title: The Strafexpedition
text: Austria attacks Italy from the Trentino and is held on the Asiago plateau.

title: Jutland
text: The British and German fleets meet off Jutland; Britain loses more ships but keeps command of the sea.

title: Sykes-Picot
text: Britain and France secretly agree how to divide the Ottoman Arab lands.

title: The Brusilov offensive
text: Brusilov breaks the Austrian line on a wide front, taking hundreds of thousands of prisoners.

title: The Arab Revolt
text: Sharif Hussein proclaims the Arab revolt against the Ottomans at Mecca.

title: Kitchener drowns
text: The war minister Lord Kitchener drowns when HMS Hampshire hits a mine off Orkney.

title: Phosgene at Verdun
text: Germany fires diphosgene shells at Verdun in its last push for Fort Souville.

title: The Somme

title: Romania enters

title: Romani

title: Tanks at Flers

title: Romania driven back
text: German and Austrian armies drive the Romanians out of Transylvania.

title: The prime minister shot
text: Friedrich Adler shoots Austria's prime minister Sturgkh at dinner in a Vienna hotel.

title: Douaumont retaken
text: French troops take back Fort Douaumont.

title: Franz Joseph dies

title: The Tremere mourn an age

ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Somme ends

title: Bucharest taken
text: German troops enter Bucharest.

title: Rasputin killed
text: Russian aristocrats poison, shoot and drown the healer Rasputin.

title: Lloyd George
text: Lloyd George becomes Britain's prime minister.

title: The turnip winter
text: A failed potato crop and the blockade leave Germans eating turnips; hundreds of thousands die of hunger and cold.

title: The Brno hunger
text: Brno's workers queue for bread; the mills switch to army cloth, and women replace men in the factories.

title: The Central Asian revolt
